source_refs.note: Exercise 9.2, Question 1 (book p. 272); the book prints no answers for Exercise 9.2; answers checked with sympy and the solution book

blocks.explanation:
Yeh numbers wala proof hai: left side par do \(\sin^{-1}\) angles jama ho rahe hain, aur right side par ek \(\cos^{-1}\) hai.
Diya kya hai? Do angles jin ke sines \(\frac{7}{25}\) aur \(\frac{15}{17}\) hain.
Find kya karna hai? Dikhana hai ke in ka jama woh angle hai jis ka cosine \(\frac{87}{425}\) hai.
Rule kaunsa? Jawab \(\cos^{-1}\) mein hai, is liye cosine wala jama formula (iii) lagayenge.
Plan: pehle dono angles ko right triangle ki madad se \(\cos^{-1}\) shakal mein badlenge, phir formula (iii).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\sin^{-1}\frac{7}{25}\) aur \(\sin^{-1}\frac{15}{17}\).
Maloom karna (prove): in ka jama \(\cos^{-1}\frac{87}{425}\) hai.
Tareeqa: jawab \(\cos^{-1}\) mein hai, is liye formula (iii) lagayenge: \(\cos^{-1}x + \cos^{-1}y = \cos^{-1}\left(xy - \sqrt{(1-x^{2})(1-y^{2})}\right)\). Lekin yeh formula tabhi lagta hai jab dono terms \(\cos^{-1}\) hon, is liye pehle har angle ko \(\cos^{-1}\) mein badalna hoga.

\(\sin^{-1}\frac{7}{25}\) ko \(\cos^{-1}\) mein badlein
\[\alpha = \sin^{-1}\tfrac{7}{25},\quad \sin\alpha = \tfrac{7}{25}\]
\[\cos\alpha = \sqrt{1 - \tfrac{49}{625}} = \sqrt{\tfrac{576}{625}}\]
\[= \tfrac{24}{25}\]
\[\alpha = \cos^{-1}\tfrac{24}{25}\]
Kyun: \(\sin^{2}\alpha + \cos^{2}\alpha = 1\) se cosine nikala. Sine positive hai, is liye \(\alpha\) pehle quadrant \(\left[0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) mein hai, jahan cosine bhi positive hota hai. \(\cos^{-1}\frac{24}{25}\) bhi isi interval mein hai, is liye dono ek hi angle hain. Triangle ki zubaan mein: opposite 7, hypotenuse 25, to adjacent 24 (7, 24, 25 triple).
Dhyan dein: \(\sqrt{576} = 24\) aur \(\sqrt{625} = 25\); yeh squares yaad hon to hisaab foran ho jata hai.

\(\sin^{-1}\frac{15}{17}\) ko \(\cos^{-1}\) mein badlein
\[\beta = \sin^{-1}\tfrac{15}{17},\quad \sin\beta = \tfrac{15}{17}\]
\[\cos\beta = \sqrt{1 - \tfrac{225}{289}} = \sqrt{\tfrac{64}{289}}\]
\[= \tfrac{8}{17}\]
\[\beta = \cos^{-1}\tfrac{8}{17}\]
Kyun: bilkul wohi wajah. Opposite 15, hypotenuse 17, to adjacent 8 (8, 15, 17 bhi Pythagorean triple hai). Angle pehle quadrant mein hai, is liye positive root.

Formula (iii) lagayein, \(x = \frac{24}{25},\ y = \frac{8}{17}\)
\[\sqrt{1-x^{2}} = \tfrac{7}{25},\quad \sqrt{1-y^{2}} = \tfrac{15}{17}\]
\[\text{L.H.S} = \cos^{-1}\tfrac{24}{25} + \cos^{-1}\tfrac{8}{17}\]
\[= \cos^{-1}\left(\tfrac{24}{25}\cdot\tfrac{8}{17} - \tfrac{7}{25}\cdot\tfrac{15}{17}\right)\]
Kyun: formula ke square roots asal mein wohi sines hain jin se hum ne shuru kiya tha, is liye dobara hisaab ki zaroorat nahi. Formula (iii) ki shart \(x + y \ge 0\) hai, jo yahan poori hai kyunke dono positive hain.
Dhyan dein: cosine ke jama mein beech mein minus hai, plus nahi.

Hisaab saaf karein
\[= \cos^{-1}\left(\tfrac{192}{425} - \tfrac{105}{425}\right)\]
\[= \cos^{-1}\tfrac{87}{425} = \text{R.H.S}\]
Kyun: denominator \(25 \times 17 = 425\). Numerators: \(24 \times 8 = 192\) aur \(7 \times 15 = 105\). Farq \(192 - 105 = 87\). Left side right side ke barabar ho gaya.
Is tarah humein do lambe square roots dobara nahi nikalne pare, sirf multiplication aur ek minus.

Tasdeeq
\[\sin^{-1}\tfrac{7}{25} + \sin^{-1}\tfrac{15}{17} \approx 0.2838 + 1.0808\]
\[= 1.3646\]
\[\cos^{-1}\tfrac{87}{425} \approx 1.3646\ \checkmark\]
Kyun: calculator (radian mode) dono taraf ek hi angle deta hai, is liye proof ka natija sahi hai.
